screening_results.reason: The abstract examines macro- and microstructural brain alterations in sexually assaulted women but does not state that participants were diagnosed with PTSD or that GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls were assessed (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are apparent. Insufficient information to determine eligibility from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 is not met — study used healthy subjects and experimental trauma film rather than PTSD patients compared to controls; I2 not demonstrated/applicable. Therefore excluded based on not meeting required PTSD vs control GM volume comparison.

No exclusion criteria met (exclusion IDs: []). Inclusion criterion I2 met (controls included healthy and trauma-exposed). Inclusion criterion I1 not met: the study analyzes cortical thickness-based structural covariance network centrality rather than grey matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls, as required for inclusion.

Empirical VBM MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between adolescents with PTSD (due to childhood sexual abuse) and matched non-traumatised healthy controls. This directly assesses GMV differences relevant to PTSD morphometry. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological/lesion/review) are met.

No exclusion criteria met (E1-E3). Inclusion criterion I1 not met: study examined healthy adolescents with community violence exposure, not PTSD patients vs controls. While MRI GM volume was assessed, there was no PTSD patient group for comparison. I2 not met/applicable: no trauma-exposed non-PTSD control vs PTSD comparison.

Abstract reports structural neuroimaging of posttrauma anhedonia in PTSD but does not specify whether GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls (I1) were assessed or what control group was used (I2). No exclusion criteria are evident. Insufficient information in abstract to determine eligibility, so include for full-text review.

Abstract addresses cingulo-insular volumetric alterations in relation to FND and PTSD symptoms but does not clearly report an empirical MRI comparison between PTSD patients and controls. Inclusion criterion I1 (PTSD vs controls) is not demonstrated; no exclusion criteria are apparent. Insufficient information—include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (study does not assess GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls; it compares responders vs non-responders within a PTSD sample). I2 not demonstrated (no control population reported).

Empirical English-language MRI study using T1-weighted images and voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between coal mine gas explosion-related PTSD patients (n=14) and non-traumatized controls (n=25). Meets I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria apply. Recommend full-text review for data extraction.

No comparison between PTSD patients and controls is reported; study assesses trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD only. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (does not evaluate GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls); I2 not applicable (study sample are subclinical trauma-exposed individuals, not controls in a PTSD vs control comparison).

Empirical study reporting smaller global and regional cortical gray matter volume in adult PTSD, consistent with morphometric MRI outcomes comparing PTSD patients to controls. No exclusion criteria met. Abstract does not specify control type but meets inclusion criterion for MRI grey matter volume comparison; include for full-text review to confirm methods and control details.

Abstract reports structural GMV measures and includes healthy/non-PTSD control groups, but does not clearly report GMV differences between PTSD patients and controls (I1 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine I1 from abstract alone; include for full-text review to confirm morphometry group comparisons.

Empirical MRI morphometry study comparing hippocampal grey matter volume in children/adolescents with PTSD versus non-maltreated control subjects. Satisfies I1 (MRI assessment of GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (healthy/non-maltreated control group). No exclusion criteria (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

The study reports VBM in borderline personality disorder (BPD) patients vs healthy controls and only uses lifetime PTSD as a covariate. It does not assess gray-matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls, so inclusion criterion I1 is not met. I2 (control type) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are met.

Abstract reports morphovolumetric (structural) changes in 19 drug-naïve PTSD patients compared with 19 healthy controls after EMDR; no exclusions evident (no drugs, lesions, or review). MRI modality/explicit GM-volume statement is not clearly stated in the abstract, so full-text review is required to confirm I1.

Abstract investigates brain volume reductions in child abuse-related complex PTSD, implying structural morphometry, and compares to classic PTSD findings. However, it does not explicitly state MRI methods or specify the control group type. No exclusion criteria are met. Because inclusion criteria (I1 and I2) are plausible but not clearly demonstrated from the abstract alone, INCLUDE for full-text review to confirm MRI methods and control comparisons.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (controls are healthy/trauma-exposed). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study reporting anterior cingulate gray matter volume differences between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls (victims without PTSD); no exclusion criteria met.

Title and abstract indicate a volumetric study of the superior temporal gyrus in maltreated children/adolescents with PTSD, which aligns with morphometry of structural alterations in PTSD. Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between combat veterans with PTSD and trauma-exposed controls; no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review. Meets I1 and I2; exclusion criteria not met.

Abstract reports rACC volume predicting CBT treatment response in PTSD but does not state comparisons between PTSD patients and control groups or explicit GM volume difference analyses. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 — study does not compare PTSD patients with controls; it examines genetic effects in a healthy non-clinical sample. Abstract describes an empirical MRI morphometry study reporting decreased premotor cortex grey matter volume in PTSD patients compared to controls following urban violence, satisfying I1. Include for full-text review to confirm control characteristics and analytic details.

Empirical English-language MRI study using Voxel-Based Morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between PTSD patients and both healthy and trauma-exposed controls. No pharmacological manipulations, lesions, or review methods reported. Full-text review appropriate.

Study examines hippocampal volume changes with age/gender in healthy young adults; no PTSD patient group or PTSD vs control comparison. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E3 not met). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (no MRI comparison of PTSD patients and controls); I2 not applicable (no PTSD group).

No exclusion criteria met. No exclusion criteria met. No exclusion criteria met (exclusion IDs: none). Inclusion criteria met: none. Study does not involve PTSD patients or compare PTSD cases vs controls. No exclusion criteria met (E1-E3). Inclusion criteria: I1 not met — not an MRI study comparing PTSD patients and controls; I2 not demonstrated/applicable — although healthy controls are acceptable, there is no PTSD group. Empirical Voxel-based morphometry MRI study including a PTSD group (n=91) and healthy controls, assessing gray matter volume differences; meets I1 and I2. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review—no exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract PTSD-specific effect sizes and subgroup details.

No control group or between-group GM volume comparison reported in abstract. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no comparison of PTSD patients vs controls reported), I2 (no control population described).

Empirical English-language structural MRI (3T) voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between pediatric PTSD patients (n=27) and healthy non-traumatized controls (n=27). No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review. Satisfies I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria met.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing hippocampal and anterior cingulate grey matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls; no exclusion criteria met and it addresses structural GM alterations in PTSD.

Abstract reports an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes in recent-onset PTSD patients versus trauma-exposed controls and non-trauma controls, matching inclusion criteria. Abstract reports longitudinal changes in hippocampal gray matter following psychological treatment for combat-related PTSD, suggesting GM morphometry was measured. Abstract examines gray matter volume in OEF/OIF veterans and links deployment/post-deployment experiences to structural brain changes, but does not explicitly state MRI methods nor report comparisons between PTSD patients and controls. Empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls, matching inclusion criteria (I1, I2). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are indicated in the abstract. Full text should be reviewed for details.

Empirical structural MRI study reporting reduced left occipital gray matter volume in male combat veterans with PTSD relative to veterans without PTSD. Meets I1 (GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I2 (controls are trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD). No exclusion criteria are met (not pharmacological, not a lesion study, not a review). Include for full-text review.

Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Empirical structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing gray matter volumes between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls (combat veterans). Meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (controls are trauma-exposed without PTSD). No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review is reported. This is an empirical MRI volumetric study comparing grey matter volumes in maltreated youth with chronic PTSD, maltreated youth without PTSD (trauma-exposed controls), and nonmaltreated controls, meeting I1 and I2. No exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical MRI study comparing hippocampal volumes in well-characterized chronic PTSD patients versus control subjects, matching inclusion criteria for GM volume assessment (I1) and use of control population (I2). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review) are indicated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract effect sizes and methods.

Empirical MRI study using region-based morphometry and DTI comparing 44 PTSD patients to both trauma-exposed controls and healthy controls; reports gray matter volume differences. No exclusions apparent (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review). Full-text review appropriate to extract detailed morphometry data.

Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray-matter volume between PTSD patients (n=9) and trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=16). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between cancer survivors with PTSD and two control groups (cancer survivors without PTSD and healthy subjects). Empirical MRI morphometry study using ROI and VBM to compare grey matter (hippocampal) volumes between PTSD patients and normal controls; subjects were non-substance-abusing. Abstract reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter volume (GMV) between PTSD patients and healthy controls (meets I1) and uses healthy/trauma-exposed control groups (meets I2). No pharmacological manipulations, lesion methods, or review article features are reported (no exclusion criteria met). Full-text review appropriate to confirm details.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (trauma-exposed controls without PTSD). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 — the abstract reports cortical thickness analysis (shape/thickness), not grey matter volume differences; volumetric GM comparisons are not demonstrated. Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between recent-onset PTSD patients (n=10) and trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=10). No pharmacological manipulation or lesion study; directly assesses GM differences, meeting I1 and I2.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I1 and I2 not demonstrated — study reports longitudinal GM density changes and comparisons between recovered vs symptomatic PTSD patients, but lacks comparisons to healthy or trauma-exposed non-PTSD control groups.

Abstract reports voxel-based morphometry and Freesurfer analyses of between-group volumetric differences in traumatized adolescents with and without PTSD, indicating MRI-based grey matter volume comparisons between PTSD cases and trauma-exposed controls. No pharmacological, lesion, or review study aspects are indicated.

Abstract reports MRI/MRS investigation of hippocampal structural abnormalities in fire victims with recent-onset PTSD but does not explicitly state GM volume comparisons or the control group. No exclusion criteria apparent. Include for full-text review to confirm I1 and I2.

Abstract reports investigation of PTSD-related structural alterations consistent with morphometry objectives, but does not explicitly state MRI, gray matter volume measures, or details of control group. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient methodological detail for definitive inclusion, so include for full-text review to confirm MRI-based GM comparisons.

Empirical English-language MRI study measuring hippocampal (GM) volumes in drug-naïve PTSD patients versus matched healthy controls, with no pharmacological manipulations or lesion focus. Satisfies I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria met.

sMRI study comparing gray matter volume and density between 24 pediatric PTSD patients and 24 age- and gender-matched controls, meeting inclusion criteria for MRI assessment of GM differences and appropriate control group. No exclusion criteria (pharmacologic manipulation, lesion study, or review) are met.

Abstract reports an empirical morphometric (gray matter) brain study using monozygotic twin pairs discordant for combat exposure to compare PTSD cases and controls. This satisfies I1 (MRI grey matter volume differences) and I2 (appropriate control population). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets I1 and I2: empirical English MRI study assessing cortical gray matter volume differences between 25 drug‑naive adult PTSD patients and 25 matched non‑traumatized controls using SIENAX and VBM. No pharmacological manipulations, not a lesion study or review. Include for full-text review.

MRI study comparing normalized brain and subcortical volumes between 9 TR-PTSD patients and 10 healthy volunteers, reporting significant GM and hippocampal volume differences. Meets I1 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I2 (healthy control group). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are indicated in the abstract. Recommend full-text review for data extraction.

Title and abstract indicate voxel-based and volumetric analyses of the anterior cingulate cortex in individuals with acute PTSD, consistent with an empirical MRI morphometry study comparing PTSD patients to controls; no exclusion criteria are evident. Full text needed to confirm control population details and exact GM volume measures.

Empirical MRI study comparing amygdala (GM) volumes between individuals with history of PTSD and trauma-exposed controls; aligns with review objective of morphometry studies of structural alterations in PTSD. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological/lesion/review) are met in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between PTSD patients (fire survivors) and trauma-exposed controls. No pharmacological manipulation, not a lesion study, and not a review. Meets I1 and I2; exclusion criteria not met.
